summary: Intermittent inference request timeouts and 502s caused by LB idle-close + oversized cookie headers
description:
Issue summary:
ParkView reported intermittent inference requests returning 502 or timing out after ~60s for long-running streaming/batched requests. Errors started 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC, affecting ~4% of requests for this customer. Impact: customer-facing production endpoints experienced degraded availability for inference-heavy endpoints (batch infer + streaming sessions).

Impact:
- Customer observed spikes in error rates and client-side timeouts during large-batch jobs and some streaming sessions.
- Business impact: several analytics jobs failed and triggered support alerts.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east with reserved capacity (dedicated infra).
- Requests route through our external ELB -> nginx ingress -> api-gateway -> serving runtime.

Observed symptoms:
- 502 and connection reset seen in client logs.
- Server-side logs show upstream request terminated by nginx with "upstream prematurely closed connection" and occasional "header too large" warnings in ingress.
- Errors correlate to requests with large Cookie headers (customer uses large session cookie for their proxy).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use ParkView prod tenant and send a long-running streaming request (payload + multi-turn) or a large batch infer POST (~2-3MB body with long context).
2) Include an oversized Cookie header (20-40KB including custom session metadata).
3) Observe response: after ~60s many sessions receive 502 or the client observes a timeout.
4) Repeat with smaller cookies and shorter requests to confirm reduced failure rate.
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage by Support (Aisha): confirmed customer stack and repro pattern; gathered request IDs and timestamps.
- SRE (Marcus) pulled ingress/nginx logs and ELB metrics. Found repeated 'upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header' and 'client intended to send too large header' messages.
- Correlation: 502s cluster around requests where nginx logged header-size warnings; timeouts cluster at ~60s which matches ELB idle_timeout default.
- Hypotheses considered:
  * Serving runtime OOM/worker crash — ruled out (no corresponding container restarts, runtime metrics OK).
  * Model inference perf regression — ruled out for majority of requests; p99 compute remained consistent.
  * Network/LB timeout + proxy buffering and large headers causing premature connection closing — matches logs and customer headers.
- Confirmed that our ELB has a 60s idle timeout and nginx has default proxy_buffering enabled and default large_header buffers (smaller than customer cookie).
- When proxy_buffering is enabled, nginx reads the full upstream response into buffers; combined with ELB idle timeout and slow first-byte from a long-tail model run the ELB closes the connection if it sees no activity for 60s. With large request headers nginx returns 502 when header size exceeds configured limits.
logs:
2026-03-10T14:12:07Z nginx[ingress]: [error] 12345#0: *98765 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 203.0.113.12, server: api.redwood.example, request: "POST /v1/infer HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.12.45:8080/", host: "parkview.prod.redwood.com"
2026-03-10T14:12:07Z nginx[ingress]: [warn] 12345#0: *98765 a client request body is buffered to a temp file /var/cache/nginx/client_body/0000001234, client: 203.0.113.12, server: api.redwood.example
2026-03-10T14:12:07Z elb: Idle timeout exceeded (60s) for request id: req-0a1b2c
2026-03-10T14:12:07Z nginx[ingress]: [error] 12345#0: *98766 client intended to send too large header, client: 203.0.113.12, server: api.redwood.example
resolution:
Workaround and fix applied: 
1) Immediate workaround (2026-03-10 15:00 UTC): Support advised ParkView to trim session cookies (remove large metadata) and retry streaming jobs; error rate dropped to near zero for those sessions.
2) Short-term infra mitigation (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC): SRE increased ELB idle timeout from 60s -> 120s for the dedicated tenant routing. This reduced idle-timeout-induced disconnects for long-tail inference.
3) Mid-term config change (2026-03-11 18:30 UTC): Deployed nginx ingress config change for the dedicated tenant: increased large_client_header_buffers to 8 16k and client_header_buffer_size to 16k, and disabled proxy_buffering for inference routes to allow streaming passthrough. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/291.
4) Long-term: Created internal task INT-4204 to standardize header buffer and idle timeout settings for dedicated tenants and to add a check in onboarding docs to warn about large cookies.

Post-change validation: After config changes and customer cookie trimming, error rate dropped from ~4% -> 0.3% and no further 502 clusters observed in 48h post-rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:45 UTC - Aisha Raman (Support): Collected request IDs from customer and confirmed hit patterns. Forwarding to SRE with logs.

2026-03-10 15:20 UTC - Marcus Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally with oversized Cookie header. Nginx returns header-too-large; ELB closes idle connections at 60s. Hypothesis: combined effect of large headers + default LB idle timeout + proxy buffering is causing timeouts and 502s.
2026-03-10 16:05 UTC - Aisha Raman (Support): Shared temporary mitigation with ParkView (trim cookies), customer confirmed immediate improvement for test runs.

2026-03-11 02:15 UTC - Marcus Chen (SRE): Increased ELB timeout to 120s for affected routing. Monitoring shows fewer connection resets but header errors persisted for some requests; prepared nginx buffer changes.

2026-03-11 19:00 UTC - Marcus Chen (SRE): Deployed nginx config update and disabled proxy_buffering on /v1/infer for dedicated tenant. Running canary traffic looks good. Opening INT-4204 to make infra-wide standard.
2026-03-12 09:10 UTC - ParkView (Customer): Confirmed production jobs completed without errors after changes. Thank you for quick turnaround.
